review_notes:
I read all of Supported.lean. I also read Reduction/Cube.lean and Fourier/Fourier.lean (the definitions of Cube, mean, noise, fourier, synth, bit, degree, flip and diff), and the start of Fourier/Walsh.lean. I grepped Mathlib for Walsh, noise-operator and influence concepts and found no matching development of Boolean-function analysis, so there is nothing to integrate with.

The file's new definitions are Supported, walsh, truncate and influence.
- Supported is a one-line predicate: every set bit of s lies in S. It has no real Mathlib counterpart, because Cube n is a custom iterated Bool × Cube n type rather than Fin n → Bool, so Finset.support and hammingNorm do not apply directly.
- truncate and influence are specific to this development. influence is the mean of |diff|, built on mean, which is a thin wrapper around Finset.expect.
- degree_eq_sum is a lemma, not a definition, so I excluded it.

walsh here, defined by recursion on Cube n, does have a parallel in the repo: IndependentSetsGames.Foundations.Hastad.walsh in Fourier/Walsh.lean, defined on I → Bool as a product of bitSign. That duplicate sits in a different namespace and uses a different Cube representation. It is internal to the repo, not a competing Mathlib concept, and merging it would mean changing the Cube representation. I did not report it, since the rubric concerns concepts already in Mathlib, core or Batteries.

I am fairly confident in the result. The remaining uncertainty is whether Mathlib's finite-abelian-group Fourier machinery (AddChar and ZMod characters) could replace walsh. The custom recursive Cube type makes any such replacement a large refactor, and I could not show a concrete benefit.
